item.title: Black Hole Flare Is Biggest and Most Distant Seen
item.description:
📝 The supermassive black hole behind the flare is a type of accreting, or feeding, black hole called an active galactic nucleus (AGN). This phenomenon occurs when a supermassive black hole's gravity shears a star that comes too close, slowly consuming the star over time as it spirals into the black hole. If the flare is from a TDE, the scientists estimate that the supermassive black hole gobbled a star with a mass at least 30 times greater than that of our Sun.
🔗 Read more: https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/black-hole-flare-is-biggest-and-most-distant-seen
